Wu Shiquan 吳仕詮 (courtesy name Ziyong 子用, third in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month) was registered in a civilian household of Gui'an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a Prefectural Student who specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Wu Zhang 璋 (posthumously honored as Office Manager of a Provincial Administration Commission), his grandfather was Wu Long 龍 (County Magistrate), his father was Wu Zheng 徵 (Judicial Secretary), and his mother was Lady Gu 顧氏. His mother was living while his father had passed away. His elder brothers were Wu Shirang 仕讓 (tribute student, gongshi) and Wu Shicheng 仕誠 (National University Student); his younger brothers were Wu Shiliang 仕諒 and Wu Shixiang 仕祥 (National University Student). He married Lady Zang 臧氏. He placed forty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Peng 梁鵬 (courtesy name Kongshi 孔適, second in seniority among his brothers, aged twenty-eight, born on the second day of the tenth month) was registered in a civilian household of Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a Supernumerary Student of the Prefectural School who specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His great-grandfather was Liang Guanxian 觀賢, his grandfather was Liang Zongdao 宗道, his father was Liang Zuyin 祖寅, and his mother was Lady Tang 唐氏. Both of his parents had passed away. His elder brother was Liang E 鶚. He married Lady Zheng 鄭氏. He placed seventeenth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and one hundred forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Runing 胡汝寧 (courtesy name Wenzhen 文禎, fourth in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty-four, born on the ninth day of the eighth month) was registered in a civilian household of Nanchang County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was a County Student who specialized in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing). His great-grandfather was Hu Bingran 秉然, his grandfather was Hu Kongdao 孔道, his father was Hu Cong 聰, and his mother was Lady Dai 戴氏. His mother was living while his father had passed away. His elder brother was Hu Ruqi 汝器. He married Lady Qin 秦氏. He placed eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chenzhi 李臣之 (courtesy name Siliang 思良, first in seniority among his brothers, aged thirty, born on the eleventh day of the second month) was registered in a civilian household of Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, and was a Student of the Directorate of Education who specialized in the Classic of Changes (Yijing). His great-grandfather was Li Chun 春, his grandfather was Li Xing 興 (Investigating Censor), his father was Li Dang 黨, and his mother was Lady Si 司氏. Both of his parents were living. He married Lady Zhang 張氏. He placed fifty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and one hundred fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李大嘉〔貫山西平陽府曲沃縣匠籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字子美，行五，年三十六，正月十九日生〕。曾祖讓；祖仲賢；父臻，母田氏。永感下。兄選、大相、大禄、大剛。娶辛氏。山西鄉試第五十九名，會試第三百一名。

任養心〔貫山西平陽府解州芮城縣軍籍，縣學生，治《易經》，字子誠，行二，年二十八，四月初五日生〕。曾祖幹；祖景武〔壽官〕；父良士〔冠帶生員〕，母周氏。重慶下。兄養性，弟養廉、養氣、養蒙、養德。娶張氏。山西鄉試第六十名，會試第二百三十八名。
translation_en:
Yang Yinqiu 楊寅秋 [registered in a civilian household of Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi; County School Student; specializing in the Classic of Rites (Liji); courtesy name Yishu 義叔; second in generational seniority; aged twenty-eight; born on the ninth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Yang Zongming 宗明 [Official Student (guansheng)]; his grandfather was Yang Siyao 思堯; his father was Yang Shaozu 紹祖; his father's first wife was née Xiao 蕭, and his mother is née Xiao 蕭. His mother is living while his father is deceased (cishixia). His elder brother is Yang Yinchun 寅春, and his younger brothers are Yang Yindong 寅冬 and Yang Yinming 寅命. He married née Liang 梁. He placed 76th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 64th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jing 吳澋 [registered in an artisan household of Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi; National University Student (guozisheng); specializing in the Classic of Documents (Shujing); courtesy name Wenhuan 文煥; eighth in generational seniority; aged thirty-nine; born on the eighth day of the fourth month]. His great-grandfather was Wu Dabang 大邦; his grandfather was Wu Zhen 珍; his father was Wu 𨱑 [District Magistrate], his legal mother was née Zhang 張, and his birth mother was née Xu 徐. Both his parents are deceased (yongganxia). His elder brothers are Wu Jin 溍 [Treasury Official], Wu Hao 灝, Wu Kuai 澮, Wu Zhang 漳, Wu Bin 瀕 [Subordinate Sacrificial Attendant (shengji guan)], Wu Zhun 準, and Wu Qian 潛. He married née Xu 徐. He placed 87th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 81st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Dajia 李大嘉 [registered in an artisan household of Quwo County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; County School Student; specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zimei 子美; fifth in generational seniority; aged thirty-six; born on the nineteenth day of the first month]. His great-grandfather was Li Rang 讓; his grandfather was Li Zhongxian 仲賢; his father was Li Zhen 臻, and his mother was née Tian 田. Both his parents are deceased (yongganxia). His elder brothers are Li Xuan 選, Li Daxiang 大相, Li Dalu 大禄, and Li Dagang 大剛. He married née Xin 辛. He placed 59th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Yangxin 任養心 [registered in a military household of Ruicheng County, Xiezhou Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi; County School Student; specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Zicheng 子誠; second in generational seniority; aged twenty-eight; born on the fifth day of the fourth month]. His great-grandfather was Ren Gan 幹; his grandfather is Ren Jingwu 景武 [Honorary Elder (shouguan)]; his father is Ren Liangshi 良士 [Student Awarded Cap and Sash (guandai shengyuan)], and his mother is née Zhou 周. Both his parents and grandparents are living (chongqingxia). His elder brother is Ren Yangxing 養性, and his younger brothers are Ren Yanglian 養廉, Ren Yangqi 養氣, Ren Yangmeng 養蒙, and Ren Yangde 養德. He married née Zhang 張. He placed 60th in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
梁必強〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣民籍縣學附學生治詩經字柔可行三年二十八十二月二十九日生〕
曾祖華祖聰父廷棟母許氏
永感下兄必試必大雲龍〔貢士〕弟必端娶張氏
廣東鄉試第六十名會試第九十九名
赫瀛〔貫直隸大名府濬縣民籍縣學生治書經字登甫行二年三十八月二十二日生〕
曾祖忠祖明父蘭嫡母路氏生母盧氏
永感下兄洲娶趙氏
順天府鄉試第四十五名會試第一百六名
===
郝國章〔貫太醫院官籍山西太原府陽曲縣人順天府學生治易經字廷符行一年三十一九月二十五日生〕
曾祖榮〔太醫院院判〕祖儒〔太醫院醫士〕父鉞〔太醫院醫士〕母郭氏
慈侍下弟國奇〔太醫院醫士〕娶楊氏
順天府鄉試第一百十二名會試第二百四十一名
阮子孝〔貫浙江杭州府於潛縣民籍縣學生治詩經字伯慕行五年三十三八月二十一日生〕
曾祖玒祖浦父栴母金氏繼母盛氏
永感下兄子芳子厚子充子儀弟子重子陵娶趙氏
浙江鄉試第十二名會試第一百五十五名
alt_text:
梁必強
貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣民籍　縣學附學生
治詩經字秉可行三年二十八十二月二十九日生
曾祖華　祖聰　父廷棟　母許氏
永感下　兄必試　必大〔雲龍貢士〕　弟必端　娶張氏
廣東鄉試第六十名　會試第九十九名
赫瀛
貫直隸大名府濬縣民籍　縣學生
治書經字登甫行二年三十八月二十二日生
曾祖忠　祖明　父蘭　嫡母路氏　生母盧氏
永感下　兄洲　娶趙氏
順天府鄉試第四十五名　會試第一百六名
===
郝國章
貫太醫院官籍山西太原府陽曲縣人　順天府學生
治易經字廷符行一年三十一九月二十五日生
曾祖榮〔太醫院院判〕　祖儒〔太醫院醫士〕　父鉞〔太醫院醫士〕　母郭氏
慈侍下　弟國奇〔太醫院醫士〕　娶楊氏
順天府鄉試第一百十二名　會試第二百四十一名
阮子孝
貫浙江杭州府於潛縣民籍　縣學生
治詩經字伯慕行五年三十三八月二十一日生
曾祖玒　祖浦　父楠　母金氏　繼母盛氏
永感下　兄子芳子厚子充子儀弟子重子陵　娶趙氏
浙江鄉試第十二名　會試第一百五十五名
punctuated:
梁必強〔貫廣東瓊州府瓊山縣民籍，縣學附學生，治《詩經》，字柔可，行三，年二十八，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖華；祖聰；父廷棟，母許氏。永感下。兄必試、必大、雲龍〔貢士〕；弟必端。娶張氏。廣東鄉試第六十名，會試第九十九名。

赫瀛〔貫直隸大名府濬縣民籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字登甫，行二，年三十，八月二十二日生〕。曾祖忠；祖明；父蘭，嫡母路氏，生母盧氏。永感下。兄洲。娶趙氏。順天府鄉試第四十五名，會試第一百六名。

郝國章〔貫太醫院官籍，山西太原府陽曲縣人，順天府學生，治《易經》，字廷符，行一，年三十一，九月二十五日生〕。曾祖榮〔太醫院院判〕；祖儒〔太醫院醫士〕；父鉞〔太醫院醫士〕，母郭氏。慈侍下。弟國奇〔太醫院醫士〕。娶楊氏。順天府鄉試第一百十二名，會試第二百四十一名。

阮子孝〔貫浙江杭州府於潛縣民籍，縣學生，治《詩經》，字伯慕，行五，年三十三，八月二十一日生〕。曾祖玒；祖浦；父栴，母金氏，繼母盛氏。永感下。兄子芳、子厚、子充、子儀；弟子重、子陵。娶趙氏。浙江鄉試第十二名，會試第一百五十五名。
translation_en:
Liang Biqiang 梁必強 [registered in Qiongshan County 瓊山縣, Qiongzhou Prefecture 瓊州府, Guangdong, under a civilian household; a supernumerary student of the county school; specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Rouke 柔可; third in seniority among brothers; aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Liang Hua 梁華, his grandfather was Liang Cong 梁聰, his father was Liang Tingdong 梁廷棟, and his mother was née Xu 許氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Liang Bishi 梁必試, Liang Bida 梁必大, and Liang Yunlong 梁雲龍 [Tribute Student (gongshi)], and his younger brother is Liang Biduan 梁必端. He is married to née Zhang 張氏. He placed 60th in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 99th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Ying 赫瀛 [registered in Xun County 濬縣, Daming Prefecture 大名府, Zhili, under a civilian household; a student of the county school; specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Dengfu 登甫; second in seniority among brothers; aged thirty, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was He Zhong 赫忠, his grandfather was He Ming 赫明, his father was He Lan 赫蘭, his legal mother was née Lu 路氏, and his birth mother was née Lu 盧氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brother is He Zhou 赫洲. He is married to née Zhao 趙氏. He placed 45th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hao Guozhang 郝國章 [registered under an official household of the Directorate of Imperial Medicine (Taiyiyuan), originally from Yangqu County 陽曲縣, Taiyuan Prefecture 太原府, Shanxi; a student of the Shuntian Prefectural School; specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Tingfu 廷符; first in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Hao Rong 郝榮 [Administrative Assistant (yuanpan) in the Directorate of Imperial Medicine], his grandfather was Hao Ru 郝儒 [Physician (yishi) in the Directorate of Imperial Medicine], his father was Hao Yue 郝鉞 [Physician in the Directorate of Imperial Medicine], and his mother is née Guo 郭氏. His mother is living. His younger brother is Hao Guoqi 郝國奇 [Physician in the Directorate of Imperial Medicine]. He is married to née Yang 楊氏. He placed 112th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ruan Zixiao 阮子孝 [registered in Yuqian County 於潛縣, Hangzhou Prefecture 杭州府, Zhejiang, under a civilian household; a student of the county school; specializing in the Classic of Poetry (Shijing); courtesy name Bomu 伯慕; fifth in seniority among brothers; aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Ruan Hong 阮玒, his grandfather was Ruan Pu 阮浦, his father was Ruan Zhan 阮栴, his mother was née Jin 金氏, and his stepmother was née Sheng 盛氏. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Ruan Zifang 阮子芳, Ruan Zihou 阮子厚, Ruan Zichong 阮子充, and Ruan Ziyi 阮子儀, and his younger brothers are Ruan Zizhong 阮子重 and Ruan Ziling 阮子陵. He is married to née Zhao 趙氏. He placed 12th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 155th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
張夢蟾〔貫直隸鳳陽府壽州衛旗籍順天府宛平縣人國子生治易經字應光行一年三十四八月十一日生〕
曾祖禮〔壽官〕祖璉〔贈知縣〕父沛〔衛知事〕母王氏
嚴侍下弟夢蛟娶徐氏繼娶孫氏
應天府鄉試第六名會試第一百五十名
張問達〔貫四川成都府內江縣民籍縣學生治書經字德孚行三年二十七九月初八日生〕
曾祖愷祖楠父克臣母胡氏
具慶下兄問仁問政弟問行娶周氏
四川鄉試第四十九名會試第二百六十三名
===
袁應祺〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣竈籍國子生治易經字文穀行四年三十三十二月二十七日生〕
曾祖傑祖潤〔知府〕父孟龍〔知州〕母錢氏
慈侍下兄應薦〔監生〕應辰應銓弟應麟應授應登應黻應擢應繡娶紀氏
順天府鄉試第七名會試第八十名
嵇應科〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍無錫縣人國子生治書經字文甫行一年三十五十月十八日生〕
曾祖祥祖浩父大有母吳氏
慈侍下弟應元娶姚氏繼娶華氏
應天府鄉試第一百一名會試第六十二名
alt_text:
張夢蟾
貫直隸鳳陽府壽州衛旗籍順天府宛平縣人國子生
治易經字應光行一年三十四八月十一日生
曾祖禮〔壽官〕　祖璉〔贈知縣〕　父沛〔衛知事〕　母王氏
嚴侍下　弟夢蛟　娶徐氏　繼娶孫氏

貫四川成都府内江縣民籍　縣學生
治書經字徳孚行三年二十七九月初八日生
曾祖愷　祖楠　父克臣　母胡氏
具慶下　兄問仁　問政　弟問行　娶周氏
四川鄉試第四十九名　會試第二百六十三名
===
袁應祺
貫直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣竈籍　國子生
治易經字文穀行四年三十三十二月二十七日生
曾祖傑　祖潤〔知府〕　父孟龍〔知州〕　母錢氏
慈侍下　兄應薦〔臨生〕　應晨　應銓　弟應麟　應授　應登　應繖　應擢　應繡　娶紀氏
順天府鄉試第七名　會試第八十名
嵇應科
貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍無錫縣人　國子生
治書經字文甫行一年三十五十月十八日生
曾祖祥　祖浩　父大有　母吳氏
慈侍下　弟應元　娶姚氏　繼娶華氏
應天府鄉試第一百一名　會試第六十二名
punctuated:
張夢蟾〔貫直隸鳳陽府壽州衛旗籍，順天府宛平縣人，國子生，治《易經》，字應光，行一，年三十四，八月十一日生〕。曾祖禮〔壽官〕，祖璉〔贈知縣〕，父沛〔衛知事〕，母王氏。嚴侍下。弟夢蛟。娶徐氏，繼娶孫氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百五十名。

張問達〔貫四川成都府內江縣民籍，縣學生，治《書經》，字德孚，行三，年二十七，九月初八日生〕。曾祖愷，祖楠，父克臣，母胡氏。具慶下。兄問仁、問政，弟問行。娶周氏。四川鄉試第四十九名，會試第二百六十三名。

袁應祺〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州興化縣竈籍，國子生，治《易經》，字文穀，行四，年三十三，十二月二十七日生〕。曾祖傑，祖潤〔知府〕，父孟龍〔知州〕，母錢氏。慈侍下。兄應薦〔監生〕、應辰、應銓，弟應麟、應授、應登、應黻、應擢、應繡。娶紀氏。順天府鄉試第七名，會試第八十名。

嵇應科〔貫直隸常州府武進縣民籍，無錫縣人，國子生，治《書經》，字文甫，行一，年三十五，十月十八日生〕。曾祖祥，祖浩，父大有，母吳氏。慈侍下。弟應元。娶姚氏，繼娶華氏。應天府鄉試第一百一名，會試第六十二名。
translation_en:
Zhang Mengchan 張夢蟾 [registered under a hereditary military officer household in the Shouzhou Guard of Fengyang Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili), originally from Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture; a Student of the Directorate of Education (guozisheng) specializing in the Classic of Changes (Yijing); courtesy name Yingguang; first in his generation; aged thirty-four, born on the eleventh day of the eighth month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Li [Honorary Official Held in Respect for His Age (shouguan)]; his grandfather was Zhang Lian [posthumously honored as District Magistrate]; his father is Zhang Pei [Administrative Clerk of a Guard]; his mother was née Wang. His father is living and his mother is deceased. He has a younger brother, Mengjiao. He married née Xu, and later married née Sun. He ranked 6th in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 150th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenda 張問達 [registered in a commoner household of Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan; a County Student (xian xuesheng) specializing in the Classic of History (Shujing); courtesy name Defu; third in his generation; aged twenty-seven, born on the eighth day of the ninth month]. His great-grandfather was Zhang Kai; his grandfather was Zhang Nan; his father is Zhang Kechen; his mother is née Hu. Both of his parents are living. He has elder brothers Wenren and Wenzheng, and a younger brother, Wenxing. He married née Zhou. He ranked 49th in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yuan Yingqi 袁應祺 [registered in a saltern household of Xinghua County, Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Changes; courtesy name Wengu; fourth in his generation; aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month]. His great-grandfather was Yuan Jie; his grandfather was Yuan Run [Prefect]; his father was Yuan Menglong [Subprefectural Magistrate]; his mother is née Qian. His mother is living and his father is deceased. He has elder brothers Yingjian [Directorate Student (jiansheng)], Yingchen, and Yingquan, and younger brothers Yinglin, Yingshou, Yingdeng, Yingfu, Yingzhuo, and Yingxiu. He married née Ji. He ranked 7th in the Shuntian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 80th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ji Yingke 嵇應科 [registered in a commoner household of Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area, originally from Wuxi County; a Student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of History; courtesy name Wenfu; first in his generation; aged thirty-five, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month]. His great-grandfather was Ji Xiang; his grandfather was Ji Hao; his father was Ji Dayou; his mother is née Wu. His mother is living and his father is deceased. He has a younger brother, Yingyuan. He married née Yao, and later married née Hua. He ranked 101st in the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination and 62nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:

Fang Fan 方範 (registered in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area, under a civilian household; County Student; specialized in the Record of Rites [Liji]; courtesy name Xudao; third in generational order; age thirty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Fang Sheng (Longevity Official); his grandfather was Fang Lin (Secretary in the Ministry of Rites); his father was Fang Feng (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, advanced in prestige title to Grand Master for Court Service); his legal mother was Lady Fan (invested as Child Nurturer); and his birth mother was Lady Zhang. Both of his parents are deceased. His elder brothers are Fang Ce (Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments) and Fang Zhu (Prefectural Judge of Shuntian Prefecture). He married Lady Lu. He placed 27th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Xingzhi 郭性之 (registered in Hua Subprefecture, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi, under a military household; Subprefectural Student; specialized in the Classic of History [Shujing]; courtesy name De'an; third in generational order; age thirty-five, born on the thirteenth day of the second month). His great-grandfather was Guo Jing (County Recorder); his grandfather was Guo Congren; his father was Guo Xiu (County Recorder); and his mother is Lady Wang. His mother is living. His elder brothers are Guo Fuzhi and Guo Zaizhi, and his younger brother is Guo Mingzhi. He married Lady Dong. He placed 55th in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Jingguo 貢靖國 (registered in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Southern Metropolitan Area, under a Confucian scholar household; Prefectural Student; specialized in the Classic of Poetry [Shijing]; courtesy name Xuanzhong; second in generational order; age thirty-nine, born on the tenth day of the twelfth month). His great-grandfather was Gong Tong; his grandfather was Gong Tan; his father is Gong Ruzan (Longevity Official); and his mother was Lady Mei. His father is living. His elder brother is Gong Huiguo. He married Lady Yang. He placed 117th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
皇帝制曰朕惟自昔
哲后膺乾良弼納
誨未有不以典學
勤政為務者乃嗣
服之始尤斤斤焉
===
若伊訓說命訪落
無逸諸篇詳哉其
言之矣三代以還
强學勵精之主代
有作者然考德論

服之始尤斤斤焉
===

translation_en: The Emperor's decree reads: "We reflect that since antiquity, whenever wise sovereigns have received the Mandate of Heaven and worthy辅臣 [ministers] have offered counsel, there have been none who did not make devotion to constant study and diligence in governance their priority; and at the very beginning of their succession to the throne, they were especially attentive to this. Works such as the 'Instructions of Yi' (Yi xun), the 'Charge to Yue' (Yue ming), 'Seeking Counsel at the Beginning' (Fang luo), and 'Against Luxurious Ease' (Wu yi) have spoken of this in great detail! From the Three Dynasties onward, rulers who strove to learn and exerted themselves in governance have arisen in every age. Yet when we examine their virtue and discuss their…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:

姬姒矧曰唐虞又
有可疑者夜分講
經歲周太平御覽
隻日不廢講讀學
非不篤矣而興造
洪業顧出於馬上
得之不事詩書者
何歟衡石程書衛
士傳餐汗透御服

translation_en: … governance, they still cannot be matched with those of the Zhou [Ji 姬] and Xia [Si 姒] dynasties, let alone those of Tang 唐 [Yao 堯] and Yu 虞 [Shun 舜]. Moreover, there are matters that invite doubt: lecturing on the classics until midnight, reading through the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era (Taiping yulan 太平御覽) over the course of a year, and not neglecting lectures and readings even on odd-numbered days—such learning was certainly not lacking in earnestness; yet the founding of great dynastic enterprises instead came from those who won the empire on horseback and did not occupies themselves with the Odes (Shi 詩) and the Documents (Shu 書). Why is this? Weighing documents by the stone-weight (shi 石) to set daily quotas, having palace guards pass in meals, sweating through the imperial robes, …

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
日旰忘倦政非不
勤矣而致理之效
顧獨稱躬修玄默
清靜無為者何歟
朕以冲年履阼未
===
燭於理惟仰遵我
皇考遺命講學親賢
日勤觀覽細大之
務悉咨輔臣以求
厥中夙夜孜孜罔

日旰忘倦政非不
勤矣而致理之效
顧獨稱躬修玄默
清靜無爲者何歟
朕以沖年履阼未
===
燭於理惟仰遵我
皇考遺命講學親賢

務悉咨輔臣以求
厥中夙夜孜孜罔
punctuated: 日旰忘倦，政非不勤矣，而致理之效，顧獨稱躬修玄默、清靜無為者，何歟？朕以冲年履阼，未燭於理，惟仰遵我皇考遺命，講學親賢，日勤觀覽，細大之務，悉咨輔臣，以求厥中，夙夜孜孜，罔…
translation_en:
…and working into the late evening without wearying: their governance was certainly not lacking in diligence. Yet when it comes to the efficacy of achieving order, why is praise reserved solely for those who personally cultivated mysterious silence and practiced pure quietude and non-action?

I have ascended the throne at a tender age and am not yet enlightened in the principles of governance. I only reverently obey the testamentary charge of my Imperial Father, engaging in study, drawing close to the worthy, and diligently reading and reviewing every day. In all affairs great and small, I consult the grand secretaries in every case so as to seek the proper mean, toiling tirelessly from early morning until late at night, never…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
志論總之不越此
三端矣可得而悉
數之歟亦有可行
於今者歟尔多士
習先聖之術明當
===
世之務其為朕折
衷眾論究其指歸
典學何急立政何
先或古今異宜創
守殊軌悉茂明之
alt_text:
志論總之不越此

於今者歟尒多士
習先聖之術明當
===
世之務其爲朕折
衷衆論究其指歸
典學何急立政何
先或古今異宜創
守殊執悉茂明之
punctuated: 志論，總之不越此三端矣。可得而悉數之歟？亦有可行於今者歟？尔多士習先聖之術，明當世之務，其為朕折衷眾論，究其指歸。典學何急？立政何先？或古今異宜、創守殊軌，悉茂明之，
translation_en: …aspirations and discourses [?], in sum they do not go beyond these three essentials. Can they be enumerated in full? Are there also those among them that can be put into practice today? You assembled scholars have mastered the arts of the former sages and understand the affairs of the present age. Weigh the various arguments for Me and investigate their essential purport: What is most urgent in devoting oneself to learning? What comes first in establishing governance? Whether antiquity and the present differ in what is appropriate, or founding and maintaining follow different paths—elucidate all of this thoroughly…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
臣孫繼臯
臣對臣聞帝王之繼天以立極也學必務乎
其本而後天下之化原以端政必審乎其要
而後天下之化機以運何者人君之學非徒
以洽聞為也凝神於宥密養邃於穆清固羲
皇以來之道統所賴以衍之於無窮者也本
之弗務則不過為口耳之學而何以造於天
德之精人君之政非徒以任智為也負君師
之責立治教之宗固羲皇以來之治統所賴
以引之於不替者也要之弗審則不過為衒
===
飾之政而何以要於王道之極惟求端於本
而不徒事乎口耳之粗則愈退蔵而愈精密
本以豫內而亦以利外也聖德所以同天而
大化之原於此乎端矣惟專持其要而不徒
事乎衒飾之具則愈簡易而愈恢弘所操至
約而所及至廣也聖治所以憲天而大化之
機於此乎運矣學以基政政以顯學道合一
而不偏學務其本政舉其要事不勞而可據
自古帝王不出密沕之內而道積厥躬允底
於淵微純粹之歸不假智術之勞而事得其

臣孫繼臯。
臣對：臣聞帝王之繼天以立極也，學必務乎其本，而後天下之化原以端；政必審乎其要，而後天下之化機以運。何者？人君之學，非徒以洽聞為也，凝神於宥密，養邃於穆清，固羲皇以來之道統所賴以衍之於無窮者也。本之弗務，則不過為口耳之學，而何以造於天德之精？人君之政，非徒以任智為也，負君師之責，立治教之宗，固羲皇以來之治統所賴以引之於不替者也。要之弗審，則不過為衒飾之政，而何以要於王道之極？惟求端於本，而不徒事乎口耳之粗，則愈退蔵而愈精密，本以豫內，而亦以利外也，聖德所以同天，而大化之原於此乎端矣。惟專持其要，而不徒事乎衒飾之具，則愈簡易而愈恢弘，所操至約，而所及至廣也，聖治所以憲天，而大化之機於此乎運矣。學以基政，政以顯學，道合一而不偏；學務其本，政舉其要，事不勞而可據。自古帝王不出密沕之內，而道積厥躬，允底於淵微純粹之歸；不假智術之勞，而事得其…
translation_en:
Your servant Sun Jigao 孫繼臯.
Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that when emperors and kings succeed to Heaven in establishing the supreme standard, their learning must be devoted to its root, and only then is the source of transforming the world made upright; their governance must carefully examine its essentials, and only then is the pivot of transforming the world set in motion. Why is this? The learning of a ruler does not consist merely in broad erudition. Concentrating the spirit in quiet profundity and nurturing depth in solemn purity—this is surely that upon which the transmission of the Way since the august Fuxi 伏羲 has relied to extend endlessly. If one does not devote oneself to the root, it is no more than learning of the mouth and ear, and how could one attain the essence of Heavenly virtue? The governance of a ruler does not consist merely in relying on cleverness. Bearing the responsibilities of ruler and teacher and establishing the foundation of order and instruction—this is surely that upon which the transmission of governance since the august Fuxi has relied to be carried forward without fail. If one does not carefully examine the essentials, it is no more than governance for ostentatious display, and how could one arrive at the ultimate of the Kingly Way? Only when one seeks to rectify the root and does not merely busy oneself with the coarseness of mouth-and-ear learning will it become ever more refined and subtle the more it is stored in retirement; originally intended to prepare the inner self, it also benefits the outer realm. Thus sage virtue matches Heaven, and the source of great transformation is hereby made upright. Only when one focuses on holding fast to the essentials and does not merely busy oneself with the trappings of ostentatious display will it become ever more vast and far-reaching the simpler and easier it is; what is grasped is most concise, yet what it reaches is most broad. Thus sage governance models itself on Heaven, and the pivot of great transformation is hereby set in motion. Learning serves as the foundation for governance, and governance makes learning manifest—the Way is unified and without bias; when learning is devoted to its root and governance takes up its essentials, affairs are reliable without toil. Since antiquity, emperors and kings did not step outside the quiet unseen realm of the palace, yet the Way accumulated in their persons and truly reached the culmination of profound subtlety and pure perfection; they did not resort to the toil of cleverness and artifice, yet affairs attained their…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
理適臻於淳龐敦大之盛者此道行也况出
震維新正天命凝承之日繼離方始尤人心
屬望之初可不循其所當急者以為典學之
本擇其所當先者以為立政之要也哉欽惟
皇帝陛下
躬不世出之資
具大有為之畧
登極一詔萬方同愛戴之心
平臺一詢百辟起欽承之念
命書四箴六箴而顧諟不怠一舜典堯謨之式
===
嘉納
帝鑑圖說而披覽不忘一湯盤武几之銘近又時
經筵之御
嚴覲吏之飭盖學已勤矣政已修矣軼於唐虞
三代之隆矣乃猶不自滿假進臣等於
廷俯賜
清問首舉商周之訓次及漢唐宋君臣之事而終
策臣等以典學立政之要慎始篤初之規豈
意臣等習先聖之術明當世之務有足以裨
萬分之一者乎而臣非其人也雖然臣愚學

清問首舉商周之訓次及漢唐宋君臣之事而終
策臣等以典學立政之要慎始篤初之規豈
意臣等習先聖之術明當世之務有足以裨
萬分之一者乎而臣非其人也雖然臣愚學
punctuated: 理，適臻於淳龐敦大之盛者，此道行也。况出震維新，正天命凝承之日；繼離方始，尤人心屬望之初。可不循其所當急者以為典學之本，擇其所當先者以為立政之要也哉！欽惟皇帝陛下，躬不世出之資，具大有為之畧。登極一詔，萬方同愛戴之心；平臺一詢，百辟起欽承之念。命書《四箴》、《六箴》，而顧諟不怠，一《舜典》、《堯謨》之式；嘉納《帝鑑圖說》，而披覽不忘，一湯盤、武几之銘。近又時經筵之御，嚴覲吏之飭。盖學已勤矣，政已修矣，軼於唐、虞、三代之隆矣。乃猶不自滿假，進臣等於廷，俯賜清問，首舉商、周之訓，次及漢、唐、宋君臣之事，而終策臣等以典學、立政之要，慎始、篤初之規。豈意臣等習先聖之術，明當世之務，有足以裨萬分之一者乎？而臣非其人也。雖然，臣愚學
translation_en:
… order, thereby arriving at an era of pure, grand, and generous flourishing, it was because this Way was practiced. How much more so now, when Your Majesty emerges like thunder in the east to inaugurate a renewal, at the very day of consolidating and receiving the Mandate of Heaven; and when Your Majesty's succession to the radiance of the throne has just begun, at the very outset when human hearts fix their hopes upon you! How could one not follow what ought to be treated as urgent as the foundation for devoting oneself to learning, and select what ought to be put first as the essential point in establishing governance?

I reverently reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor personally possesses talents rarely seen in the world and is endowed with the capacity for great achievements. With a single edict upon ascending the throne, the myriad regions shared a heart of love and devotion; with a single inquiry at the Audience Hall (Pingtai), the hundred officials aroused the thought of reverent compliance. Ordering the writing out of the Four Admonitions (Sizhen) and the Six Admonitions (Liuzhen) and keeping them constantly in view without laxity is wholly in the model of the Canon of Shun and the Counsels of Yao; graciously accepting the Illustrated Mirror for Emperors (Dijian tushuo) and perusing it without forgetting is wholly like the inscriptions on Tang's washbasin and King Wu's armrest. Recently, Your Majesty has also regularly attended the Classics Mat (jingyan) and strictly admonished the officials coming for court audience. Indeed, learning is already diligent, governance is already cultivated, and it surpasses the prosperity of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties! Yet Your Majesty still does not feel self-satisfied, and has brought your servants into the court, graciously bestowing a pure inquiry: first raising the instructions of the Shang and Zhou, next touching upon the affairs of rulers and ministers in the Han, Tang, and Song, and finally questioning your servants in this policy essay on the essentials of devoting oneself to learning and establishing governance, and the rules for being cautious at the start and earnest at the outset. Could it be that Your Majesty thinks your servants, having practiced the arts of the former sages and understood the affairs of the present age, possess enough to be of help in even one part in ten thousand? Yet your servant is not such a man. Even so, in my foolishness, my learning…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
慚稽古志切攄忠敢不披瀝罄竭以對臣聞
之君者天之子也民之主也其道為往聖繼
絕學者也其責為萬世開太平者也故美玉
弗琢則射斗之光不生寶鑑弗拭則映宿之
輝不發聖人弗學則光天之德不耀甚矣哉
學之不可已也然不曰壯而好學如日中之
光少而好學如日中之陽嗣服之始學其不
尤要乎六律不具則師曠不能正五音規矩
不設則離婁不能成方圓仁政不立則堯舜
不能平天下甚矣哉政之不可已也然不曰
===
===
能慎其初如未雨之巢不慎其初如直突之
薪嗣服之始政其不尤要乎是故臨朝願學
臨政願治凡為哲后者皆然而始尤重也論
學以輔德論政以輔治凡為良弼者皆然而
始尤切也粤稽諸商太甲高宗善守成者也
臣考其初則有伊尹傅說之誨矣人紀肇修
風愆致儆非尹之所為訓王者乎遜志乃来
聰明時憲非說之所為詔王者乎臣言焉君
行焉此所以終允德而靖殷邦也故終商之
世而曰中興之令主者必推太甲高宗也載

punctuated: 慚稽古，志切攄忠，敢不披瀝罄竭以對？臣聞之：君者，天之子也，民之主也；其道為往聖繼絕學者也，其責為萬世開太平者也。故美玉弗琢，則射斗之光不生；寶鑑弗拭，則映宿之輝不發；聖人弗學，則光天之德不耀。甚矣哉，學之不可已也！然不曰「壯而好學，如日中之光；少而好學，如日中之陽」？嗣服之始，學其不尤要乎？六律不具，則師曠不能正五音；規矩不設，則離婁不能成方圓；仁政不立，則堯、舜不能平天下。甚矣哉，政之不可已也！然不曰「能慎其初，如未雨之巢；不慎其初，如直突之薪」？嗣服之始，政其不尤要乎？是故臨朝願學，臨政願治，凡為哲后者皆然，而始尤重也；論學以輔德，論政以輔治，凡為良弼者皆然，而始尤切也。粤稽諸商，太甲、高宗，善守成者也。臣考其初，則有伊尹、傅說之誨矣。「人紀肇修」、「風愆致儆」，非尹之所為訓王者乎？「遜志乃来」、「聰明時憲」，非說之所為詔王者乎？臣言焉，君行焉，此所以終允德而靖殷邦也。故終商之世，而曰中興之令主者，必推太甲、高宗也。載
translation_en:
… ashamed in examining antiquity, yet my aspiration is earnest in expressing loyalty; how could I dare not pour out my heart and exhaust my thoughts in reply?

Your servant has heard it said: The ruler is the Son of Heaven and the master of the people; his Way is to carry on the lost learning of past sages, and his responsibility is to open up peace for ten thousand generations. Therefore, if fine jade is not carved, the light that shoots to the Dipper will not be produced; if a precious mirror is not wiped, the brilliance that reflects the constellations will not shine forth; if a sage does not study, the virtue that illuminates all under heaven will not radiate. How great indeed is the necessity that learning must not cease! Yet is it not said, "To love learning in maturity is like the light of the midday sun; to love learning in youth is like the rising sun [lit. yang of the midday]"? At the beginning of succeeding to the throne, is learning not even more crucial? If the six pitch-pipes are not prepared, Shi Kuang 師曠 cannot rectify the five tones; if the compass and square are not set up, Li Lou 離婁 cannot form squares and circles; if benevolent governance is not established, Yao 堯 and Shun 舜 cannot bring peace to all under heaven. How great indeed is the necessity that governance must not cease! Yet is it not said, "Being able to be cautious at the beginning is like a nest woven before the rain; failing to be cautious at the beginning is like firewood stacked by a straight chimney"? At the beginning of succeeding to the throne, is governance not even more crucial?

Therefore, holding court and wishing to learn, attending to governance and wishing to bring order—all wise sovereigns are thus, and at the beginning it is especially weighty; discussing learning to assist virtue, discussing governance to assist order—all good chief ministers are thus, and at the beginning it is especially urgent.

Examining the Shang dynasty, Tai Jia 太甲 and Gaozong 高宗 were skilled at preserving the achievements of their predecessors. When your servant examines their beginnings, they had the instructions of Yi Yin 伊尹 and Fu Yue 傅說. "Human relationships were first cultivated" and "warnings were given against the faults of wind-like [customs]"—was this not wherewith Yin instructed the king? "Humble your will and it will come" and "the intelligent and discerning take Heaven as their pattern"—was this not wherewith Yue counselled the king? The ministers spoke of it, and the rulers practiced it; this was how they ultimately achieved sincere virtue and pacified the state of Yin. Therefore, throughout the era of the Shang, when speaking of fine rulers of restoration, one must always point to Tai Jia and Gaozong. Furthermore, …

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
稽諸周成王亦善守成者也臣考其初則有
周公之誨矣紹庭上下陟降厥家非訪落之
詩所為作乎稼穡艱難治民祗懼非無逸之
書所為戒乎臣言焉君聽焉此所以覲耿光
而揚大烈也故終周之世而曰繼述之賢君
者必推成王也然學勤矣而所以典其學者
有本政勤矣而所以立其政者有要三代以
後此義不明強學之主誠代有之而誇靡之
風盛矣光武夜分講經而昧三公之體太宗
歲周太平御覽而失兄弟之義仁宗隻日不
===
廢講讀而牽夷狄之禍乃鴻業之建反出於
不事詩書之漢高此其故何也詞章訓詁帝
王之所以為學者不在焉故學非不足務而
務非所務者固不如豁達之資之足以有為
也勵精之主誠代有之而刻覈之習興矣始
皇衡石程書而適基秦亂文帝衛士傳餐而
滋速隋亡憲宗汗透御服日旰忘倦而實釀
唐衰乃致理之效反出於清淨無為之漢文
此其故何也簿書期會帝王之所以為政者
不在焉故政非不足勤而勤非所勤者固不

punctuated:
稽諸周，成王亦善守成者也。臣考其初，則有周公之誨矣。「紹庭上下，陟降厥家」，非《訪落》之詩所為作乎？「稼穡艱難」，「治民祗懼」，非《無逸》之書所為戒乎？臣言焉，君聽焉，此所以「覲耿光而揚大烈」也。故終周之世，而曰繼述之賢君者，必推成王也。
然學勤矣，而所以典其學者有本；政勤矣，而所以立其政者有要。三代以後，此義不明。強學之主，誠代有之，而誇靡之風盛矣。光武夜分講經，而昧三公之體；太宗歲周《太平御覽》，而失兄弟之義；仁宗隻日不廢講讀，而牽夷狄之禍。乃鴻業之建，反出於不事《詩》《書》之漢高，此其故何也？詞章訓詁，帝王之所以為學者不在焉。故學非不足務，而務非所務者，固不如豁達之資之足以有為也。勵精之主，誠代有之，而刻覈之習興矣。始皇衡石程書，而適基秦亂；文帝衛士傳餐，而滋速隋亡；憲宗汗透御服，日旰忘倦，而實釀唐衰。乃致理之效，反出於清淨無為之漢文，此其故何也？簿書期會，帝王之所以為政者不在焉。故政非不足勤，而勤非所勤者，固不
translation_en:
…Looking into the Zhou dynasty, King Cheng 成王 was also one who excelled at preserving the established order. When Your servant examines the beginning of his reign, there were the teachings of the Duke of Zhou 周公. "Continuing the ways of the court above and below, ascending and descending in his house"—was this not why the ode Counseling at the Beginning (Fangluo 訪落) was composed? "The hardships of sowing and reaping" and "governing the people with reverent caution"—was this not what the document Against Luxurious Ease (Wuyi 無逸) warned about? The ministers spoke, and the ruler listened; this was how he "beheld the bright glory and揚 carried forward the great achievements." Therefore, throughout the era of the Zhou, when speaking of worthy rulers who carried on their predecessors' legacy, one must invariably point to King Cheng.

Yet even when learning is diligent, that by which learning is guided has its root; even when governance is diligent, that by which governance is established has its essentials. After the Three Dynasties, this principle became obscure. Rulers who strove at learning indeed appeared in every age, yet a trend toward ostentation and extravagance flourished. Emperor Guangwu 光武 of Han expounded the classics until midnight, yet he was blind to the proper dignity of the Three Dukes 三公; Emperor Taizong 太宗 of Song read through the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era (Taiping yulan 太平御覽) in the course of a year, yet he failed in his duty toward his brothers; Emperor Renzong 仁宗 of Song did not neglect lectures and readings on odd-numbered days, yet he was entangled in calamities brought by foreign peoples. Meanwhile, the founding of a grand enterprise came instead from Emperor Gaozu 高祖 of Han (Han Gao 漢高), who paid no heed to the Odes and the Documents. What is the reason for this? That by which emperors and kings pursue learning does not lie in literary composition and philological exegesis. Thus, it is not that learning is unworthy of effort, but that devoting effort to what should not be pursued is certainly not as good as having a broad-minded and magnanimous disposition sufficient for great achievement.

Rulers who exerted themselves in governance indeed appeared in every age, yet a habit of harshness and nitpicking arose. The First Emperor of Qin 秦始皇 weighed out documents by the stone to set his daily quota, yet this only laid the foundation for Qin's disorder; Emperor Wen 文帝 of Sui had guards pass him his meals while working, yet this only hastened the fall of Sui; Emperor Xianzong 憲宗 of Tang soaked his imperial robes with sweat and forgot his fatigue until late in the day, yet this in fact brewed the decline of Tang. Meanwhile, the achievement of orderly rule came instead from Emperor Wen 文帝 of Han (Han Wen 漢文), who practiced pure quietude and non-action. What is the reason for this? That by which emperors and kings conduct governance does not lie in routine registers and scheduled deadlines. Thus, it is not that governance is unworthy of diligence, but that being diligent in what does not merit diligence is certainly not…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
如玄默之脩之足以有效也天啓休明生我
皇上
日親講幄而寒暑之際討論不輟
日咨輔臣而細大之務委任不貳盖法天行以
勵學獨超于章句之外憲天道以出政深探
夫理道之原即商周之主不能過之雖詩書
所稱何以加焉我
二祖
八宗之丕緒真足以振揚于不墜矣顧臣伏讀
聖制有曰論者謂帝王之學與韋布不同又謂主
===
好要則百事詳臣有以見
陛下之心望道未見之心也求治無已之心也夫
帝王之學與韋布不同此程顥之言也所謂
知學之本者也主好要則百事詳此荀卿之
言也所謂知政之要者也是故往代之臣各
執其見以陳正始之謨而往代之君亦各因
其謨以裨正始之治如仲舒賢良之策析天
人也王吉變俗之論正風化也匡衡審向之
疏與夫治性六戒勸學四儀之陳崇德政也
貢禹節儉之勸先敦朴也陳寵蕩滌煩苛之

聖制有曰論者謂帝王之學與章布不同又謂主
===

言也所謂知政之要者也是故往代之臣各
執其見以陳正始之謨而往代之君亦各因
其謨以裨正始之治如仲舒賢良之策析天
人也王吉變俗之論正風化也匡衡審向之
疏與夫治性六戒勸學四儀之陳崇德政也
貢禹節儉之勸先敦朴也陳寵蕩滌煩苛之
punctuated: 如玄默之脩之足以有效也。天啓休明，生我皇上，日親講幄，而寒暑之際討論不輟；日咨輔臣，而細大之務委任不貳。盖法天行以勵學，獨超于章句之外；憲天道以出政，深探夫理道之原。即商、周之主不能過之，雖《詩》、《書》所稱何以加焉！我二祖、八宗之丕緒，真足以振揚于不墜矣。顧臣伏讀聖制有曰：「論者謂帝王之學與韋布不同，又謂主好要則百事詳。」臣有以見陛下之心，望道未見之心也，求治無已之心也。夫「帝王之學與韋布不同」，此程顥之言也，所謂知學之本者也；「主好要則百事詳」，此荀卿之言也，所謂知政之要者也。是故往代之臣，各執其見以陳正始之謨；而往代之君，亦各因其謨以裨正始之治。如仲舒賢良之策，析天人也；王吉變俗之論，正風化也；匡衡審向之疏，與夫治性六戒、勸學四儀之陳，崇德政也；貢禹節儉之勸，先敦朴也；陳寵蕩滌煩苛之
translation_en:
… as cultivating profound quietude is sufficient to achieve real results.

Heaven has ushered in an era of auspicious brilliance and brought forth Our August Emperor. Daily You attend the classics-mat lectures in person, never ceasing discussion and inquiry through winter's cold and summer's heat; daily You consult the Grand Secretaries, entrusting to them affairs both small and great without second thoughts. Indeed, You model Yourself on the ceaseless movement of Heaven to pursue learning, rising far above mere chapter-and-verse exegesis; You take the Way of Heaven as Your standard in issuing governance, probing deeply into the source of order and the Way. Even the sovereigns of the Shang and Zhou could not surpass this; even what is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of Documents (Shu)—what more could be added to it! The great patrimony of Our Two Founders and Eight Ancestors is truly enough to be uplifted and glorified without ever falling into decline.

Yet as Your servant humbly reads the Sacred Question, it states: "Commentators say that the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoner scholars in leather belts and cloth garments, and also say that when the ruler loves the essentials, all the hundred affairs are attended to in detail." From this Your servant can see that Your Majesty's mind is a mind that gazes toward the Way as though not yet having seen it, and a mind that seeks good governance without end.

Now, "the learning of emperors and kings differs from that of commoner scholars in leather belts and cloth garments"—these are the words of Cheng Hao 程顥, which is what is meant by knowing the foundation of learning. "When the ruler loves the essentials, all the hundred affairs are attended to in detail"—these are the words of Xun Qing 荀卿 [Xunzi], which is what is meant by knowing the essentials of governance. Therefore, ministers of past dynasties each held fast to their views to set forth counsels for rectifying beginnings, and sovereigns of past dynasties likewise availed themselves of those counsels to aid in the governance of rectifying beginnings. For instance, Dong Zhongshu's 董仲舒 policy essay for the Worthy and Upright (xianliang) analyzed the relationship between Heaven and man; Wang Ji's 王吉 discourse on transforming customs rectified moral teachings and habits; Kuang Heng's 匡衡 memorial on examining one's orientation, together with the presentations on the six admonitions for governing one's nature and the four models for encouraging learning, exalted virtuous governance; Gong Yu's 貢禹 exhortations to frugality put honesty and simplicity first; Chen Chong's 陳寵 proposal to wash away vexatious harshness …

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
議尚寛厚也先天間則有姚崇之十事明時
務也元祐間則有呂公著之十事飭治紀也
在治平則司馬光以三劄進重英斷也熈寧
間則程顥以稽古正學定志之說進慎趨向
也此其言則人人殊矣顧豈無上關君德而
足以為
聖脩之助下係民生而足以為
聖治之資者乎然其本則未徹也其要則未明也
本何在哉聞之上學以心下學以耳欲得其
本純心之道不可不講也要何在哉聞之用
===
人則裕自用則小欲得其要任人之道不可
不講也請因
聖問之所及而極論之
陛下終篇策臣曰典學何急立政何先或古今異
宜創守殊軌悉茂明之以副朕慎始篤初之意
臣愚以為人之一心操存舎亡其幾至可畏
也况人君之心百欲伺之一念弗純欲且乘
之以入焉其係於學之進退非眇小也必也
主敬於淵蠖之中研幾於獨知之地夜氣清
明則有常惺之法平旦好惡則有允執之功

punctuated:
議，尚寛厚也；先天間，則有姚崇之十事，明時務也；元祐間，則有呂公著之十事，飭治紀也；在治平，則司馬光以三劄進，重英斷也；熈寧間，則程顥以稽古、正學、定志之說進，慎趨向也。此其言則人人殊矣，顧豈無上關君德而足以為聖脩之助，下係民生而足以為聖治之資者乎？然其本則未徹也，其要則未明也。本何在哉？聞之上學以心，下學以耳，欲得其本，純心之道不可不講也。要何在哉？聞之用人則裕，自用則小，欲得其要，任人之道不可不講也。請因聖問之所及而極論之。

陛下終篇策臣曰：「典學何急？立政何先？或古今異宜，創守殊軌，悉茂明之，以副朕慎始篤初之意。」臣愚以為人之一心，操存舎亡，其幾至可畏也。况人君之心，百欲伺之，一念弗純，欲且乘之以入焉，其係於學之進退非眇小也。必也主敬於淵蠖之中，研幾於獨知之地；夜氣清明，則有常惺之法；平旦好惡，則有允執之功；
translation_en:
… proposal to sweep away petty harshness esteemed leniency and generosity. During the Xiantian era (712–713), there were the ten points of Yao Chong 姚崇, which clarified contemporary affairs; during the Yuanyou era (1086–1094), there were the ten points of Lü Gongzhu 呂公著, which rectified the disciplines of governance; in the Zhiping era (1064–1067), Sima Guang 司馬光 presented three memorials, emphasizing resolute decision-making; and during the Xining era (1068–1077), Cheng Hao 程顥 presented his doctrines on examining antiquity, rectifying learning, and fixing one's resolve, exercising caution over the direction to take. The words of these men differed from person to person, yet how could they fail to concern the ruler's virtue above, sufficing to aid Your Sacred Self-cultivation, and to relate to the people's livelihood below, sufficing to serve as resources for Your Sacred Governance? Nevertheless, their root was not thoroughly penetrated, and their essentials were not fully elucidated. Wherein lies the root? I have heard that the highest learning is through the mind, while the lowest learning is through the ear; if one wishes to grasp the root, the way of purifying the mind cannot go unexamined. Wherein lie the essentials? I have heard that employing others brings abundance, while relying solely on oneself brings pettiness; if one wishes to grasp the essentials, the way of entrusting responsibilities to others cannot go unexamined. Allow me to discuss this exhaustively in response to what Your Sacred Inquiry has touched upon.

At the conclusion of the question, Your Majesty asks your servant: "In engaging in constant learning, what is most urgent? In establishing governance, what comes first? Or if ancient and modern times differ in what is appropriate, and founding and preserving follow different tracks, elucidate all of this fully so as to fulfill My intention of being cautious at the start and earnest at the outset." In your servant's humble opinion, the single mind of man—held fast, it is preserved; let go, it is lost—has subtleties that are most awesome. How much more so the mind of a ruler of men, upon which a hundred desires lie in wait! If a single thought is impure, desires will seize the opportunity to enter therein; its bearing upon the advance or retreat of learning is no small matter. One must maintain reverence within the deep and tranquil recesses, and scrutinize the subtle springs of action in the realm of solitary awareness. When the night-breath is clear and bright, there is the method of constant wakefulness; when likes and dislikes arise at dawn, there is the effort of sincerely holding fast to the mean; …

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
大庭臨御則凛乎天鑒之在兹宮闈秘密則
森乎神明之若對至善為的主善為師不雜
不息允迪為期帝王為學之本或者其在是
歟譬則水焉澄之終日止見眉睫不過一撓
方圓莫辨誠不可以不慎也故曰日月久照
不改其明星辰久旋不改其度聖人久於其
道不輟其功明此以為學聖徳之所以純也
非博綜群籍藻繢是工矻矻窮年者比也臣
故以為學之有本也人之一身應務酬物其
事尚難兼也况人君之身百責萃之忠賢弗
===
任事且因之以隳焉其係於政之得失非眇
小也必也精其選於未任人之先專其任於
既得人之後姬旦在前則委心聽順山甫在
後則改容嘉納邊廷有頗牧則授之斧鉞而
不疑郡縣有龔黃則錫之璽書而不惜不聽
讒言不責近功惟和惟一以考厥成帝王為
政之要或者其在是歟譬之車馬輪轅徒飾
非人弗行造父為御一日千里誠不可以不
審也故曰千金之裘非一狐之腋大廈之才
非一丘之木太平之功非一人之畧明此以

punctuated:
大庭臨御，則凛乎天鑒之在兹；宮闈秘密，則森乎神明之若對。至善為的，主善為師，不雜不息，允迪為期。帝王為學之本，或者其在是歟？譬則水焉，澄之終日，止見眉睫；不過一撓，方圓莫辨，誠不可以不慎也。故曰：日月久照，不改其明；星辰久旋，不改其度；聖人久於其道，不輟其功。明此以為學，聖徳之所以純也，非博綜群籍、藻繢是工、矻矻窮年者比也。臣故以為學之有本也。
人之一身，應務酬物，其事尚難兼也；况人君之身，百責萃之，忠賢弗任，事且因之以隳焉，其係於政之得失，非眇小也。必也精其選於未任人之先，專其任於既得人之後。姬旦在前，則委心聽順；山甫在後，則改容嘉納。邊廷有頗、牧，則授之斧鉞而不疑；郡縣有龔、黃，則錫之璽書而不惜。不聽讒言，不責近功，惟和惟一，以考厥成。帝王為政之要，或者其在是歟？譬之車馬，輪轅徒飾，非人弗行；造父為御，一日千里，誠不可以不審也。故曰：千金之裘，非一狐之腋；大廈之才，非一丘之木；太平之功，非一人之畧。明此以
translation_en:
… when presiding over the grand court, stand in awe as though Heaven's inspection is right here; in the seclusion of the inner palace, remain solemn as though facing the gods and spirits. Take the highest good as the target and holding fast to goodness as the teacher; without admixture and without ceasing, aim at sincere practice. Does the foundation of an emperor's learning perhaps lie in this? Take water as an analogy: if you let it settle all day, it reflects eyebrows and eyelashes when still; yet with no more than a single stir, square and round can no longer be distinguished. Truly, one cannot fail to be cautious! Therefore it is said: the sun and moon shine for a long time without altering their brightness; the stars and constellations revolve for a long time without altering their measures; the sage abides for a long time in his Way without ceasing his effort. Understanding this in pursuing learning is how sagely virtue becomes pure—it is not comparable to those who broadly gather a multitude of books, labor at華麗 ornate rhetoric, and toil away year after year. Therefore your servant holds that learning has its foundation.

When a single person's body responds to affairs and deals with things, those matters are already hard to manage all at once; how much more so the person of the ruler of men, upon whom a hundred responsibilities converge! If loyal and worthy men are not entrusted with office, affairs will consequently fall into ruin; its bearing on the success or failure of governance is by no means slight. One must carefully refine their selection before employing men, and give them undivided authority after having obtained them. When Ji Dan 姬旦 [the Duke of Zhou] is in front, wholly entrust your heart to him and follow his counsel; when Zhong Shanfu 仲山甫 is behind, compose your countenance and approvingly accept his words. When the frontier garrisons have a Lian Po 廉頗 or Li Mu 李牧, grant them the battle-axes of command without hesitation; when the commanderies and counties have a Gong Sui 龔遂 or Huang Ba 黃霸, bestow imperial letters upon them without grudging. Do not listen to slanderous words, and do not demand immediate results; in harmony and unity, examine their accomplishments. Does the essential point of an emperor's governance perhaps lie in this? Take a carriage and horses as an analogy: if wheels and shafts are merely adorned, without a person they will not move; when Zaofu 造父 acts as charioteer, it covers a thousand li in a single day. Truly, one cannot fail to examine this carefully! Therefore it is said: a fur coat worth a thousand pieces of gold is not made from the underarm of a single fox; the timber for a great mansion does not come from the trees of a single hill; the achievement of Grand Peace does not come from the strategy of a single man. Understanding this in order to…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
立政聖治之所以擴也非形神獨勞屢身從事
事沾沾自好者比也臣故以為政之有要也
然要而論之則純心以為學而任人之本以
端是故有緝熈之主則四友同心有敬勝之
君則十人彙進傳曰為政在人取人以身此
之謂也任人以立政而進學之資益廣是故
有仲虺之誥則湯德丕顯有尚父之戒則武
德日休經曰朝夕納誨以輔台德此之謂也
於乎此天下之化原所以端也天下之化機
所以運也乃臣之所獻者抑有進焉以
===
陛下非常之資其於問學之際必有永貞而勿替
者故學之不純不足患也獨患夫聰明之太
過或以為商宗周王之學為不足事而求其
所不必學者焉以
陛下非常之畧其於委用之際必有善任而不疑
者故人之不任不足患也獨患夫英敏之有
餘或以為商宗周王之政為不足師而求其
所不必行者焉求其不必學則索之愈高而
失之愈遠將有務為迂闊之談以欺
陛下如王安石之惑神宗者出矣求其不必行則

立政，聖治之所以擴也，非形神獨勞、屢身從、事事沾沾自好者比也。臣故以為政之有要也。

然要而論之，則純心以為學，而任人之本以端。是故有緝熈之主，則四友同心；有敬勝之君，則十人彙進。《傳》曰：「為政在人，取人以身。」此之謂也。任人以立政，而進學之資益廣。是故有仲虺之誥，則湯德丕顯；有尚父之戒，則武德日休。《經》曰：「朝夕納誨，以輔台德。」此之謂也。於乎！此天下之化原所以端也，天下之化機所以運也。

乃臣之所獻者，抑有進焉。以陛下非常之資，其於問學之際，必有永貞而勿替者，故學之不純不足患也；獨患夫聰明之太過，或以為商宗、周王之學為不足事，而求其所不必學者焉。以陛下非常之畧，其於委用之際，必有善任而不疑者，故人之不任不足患也；獨患夫英敏之有餘，或以為商宗、周王之政為不足師，而求其所不必行者焉。求其不必學，則索之愈高而失之愈遠，將有務為迂闊之談以欺陛下，如王安石之惑神宗者出矣；求其不必行，則
translation_en:
… establish governance, this is how sacred rule is broadened; it is not comparable to exhausting one's own body and spirit alone, repeatedly attending to affairs in person, and being smugly self-satisfied over every little matter. Your servant therefore holds that in governance there is an essential principle.

Yet if we discuss it in sum, by purifying the mind to pursue learning, the foundation for employing men is made upright. Therefore, when there was a ruler of radiant and unceasing devotion, the four friends were of one mind; when there was a sovereign whose reverence prevailed over all else, the ten able ministers advanced together. The Tradition (Classic of Rites, Doctrine of the Mean) says: "Governance lies in men; men are attracted by the ruler's own person." This is what is meant. By employing men to establish governance, the resources for advancing in learning become ever broader. Therefore, because there was the Announcement of Zhonghui (Zhonghui zhi gao), the virtue of Tang was grandly manifest; because there were the admonitions of Father Shang (Shangfu, i.e., Lü Shang 呂尚), the virtue of King Wu (Wu) grew daily more splendid. The Classic (Book of Documents, Charge to Yue) says: "Morning and evening present your instructions to aid my virtue." This is what is meant. Oh! This is how the source of transformation in the realm is made upright, and how the mechanism of transformation in the realm is set in motion.

Yet what your servant has to offer goes still further. Given Your Majesty's extraordinary natural endowments, in the pursuit of inquiry and learning You will surely maintain eternal constancy without flagging; thus, that learning might not be pure is not worth worrying about. The sole worry is that, through an excess of brilliance and acuity, You might regard the learning of the high ancestors of Shang and the kings of Zhou as unworthy of pursuit, and instead seek after what need not be learned. Given Your Majesty's extraordinary strategic vision, in delegating and employing men You will surely entrust them well without suspicion; thus, that men might not be entrusted with responsibility is not worth worrying about. The sole worry is that, through a surplus of heroic shrewdness, You might regard the governance of the high ancestors of Shang and the kings of Zhou as unworthy of emulation, and instead seek after what need not be practiced. If one seeks after what need not be learned, the higher one searches the further one strays, and there will emerge men who traffic in abstruse and impractical talk to deceive Your Majesty, just as Wang Anshi 王安石 deluded Emperor Shenzong 神宗. If one seeks after what need not be practiced, then…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
更之愈急而行之愈壞將有尚為刻薄之政
以罔
陛下如公孫鞅之惑孝公者出矣此固臣愚之過
計則然而亦豈可以弗辨哉伏願我
皇上
上畏天命
下念民生以學則
皇祖之存心錄可鑑也而奉之以為訓以政則
皇祖之聖政記可法也而率之以為行無以天下
之義理皆吾晰也而厭其卑近無以天下之
===
賢才皆吾下也而待之邈絕無以安居無事
而從逸遊無以物力豐盛而興土木無以海
宇昇平而事遠夷無以安處深宮而狎近習
則道德高厚功化洋溢內恬外煕祥臻瑞應
商周不足侔矣而況漢唐宋也乎哉草莽微
臣不識忌諱干冒

商周不足侔矣而況漢唐宋也乎哉草莽微
臣不識忌諱干冐
天威無任戰慄隕越之至臣謹對
punctuated: 更之愈急，而行之愈壞，將有尚為刻薄之政以罔陛下，如公孫鞅之惑孝公者出矣。此固臣愚之過計則然，而亦豈可以弗辨哉？伏願我皇上，上畏天命，下念民生；以學則皇祖之《存心錄》可鑑也，而奉之以為訓；以政則皇祖之《聖政記》可法也，而率之以為行。無以天下之義理皆吾晰也，而厭其卑近；無以天下之賢才皆吾下也，而待之邈絕；無以安居無事而從逸遊；無以物力豐盛而興土木；無以海宇昇平而事遠夷；無以安處深宮而狎近習。則道德高厚，功化洋溢，內恬外煕，祥臻瑞應，商、周不足侔矣，而況漢、唐、宋也乎哉！草莽微臣，不識忌諱，干冒天威，無任戰慄隕越之至。臣謹對。
translation_en:
… the more urgently changes are made, the more ruined their execution becomes; then there will emerge those who advocate harsh and ungenerous policies to deceive Your Majesty, just as Gongsun Yang 公孫鞅 deluded Duke Xiao 孝公. Although this is indeed the excessive worry of your foolish servant, how could one fail to discern it?

I humbly pray that our Emperor will above stand in awe of the Mandate of Heaven, and below be mindful of the people's livelihood. With regard to learning, the Imperial Ancestor's Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu 存心錄) can serve as a mirror—revere it as your precept. With regard to governance, the Imperial Ancestor's Record of Sacred Governance (Shengzheng ji 聖政記) can serve as a model—follow it in your actions. Do not, thinking that all the moral principles under Heaven are already clear to you, grow weary of what is humble and near at hand; do not, thinking that all the worthy talents under Heaven are inferior to you, treat them with distant aloofness; do not indulge in idle excursions because you dwell in peace without incident; do not launch grand construction projects because material resources are abundant; do not engage in campaigns against distant barbarians because the realm within the seas is at peace; and do not grow overly familiar with close attendants because you reside securely deep within the palace. Then your moral virtue will be lofty and profound, your achievements and transformative influence will overflow, the court within will be tranquil and the realm without will be prosperous, and auspicious signs and felicitous omens will arrive in response. Even the Shang and Zhou dynasties will not be enough to equal you—how much less the Han, Tang, and Song!

Your rustic and humble servant, ignorant of taboos, has offended the Celestial Majesty and is overcome with the utmost trembling and fear of transgression. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
臣余孟麟
臣對臣聞帝王之建極以綏猷也有立天下
之大本有圖天下之大機大本者何明義理
以養其心而典學之為急大機者何擴紀法
以經其治而勤政之為先然遜志時敏允懷
于茲非古之所謂典學乎而學之所當急者
貴識其要宣序糾虔朝夕無怠非古之所謂
勤政乎而政之所當先者貴得其綱此則本
之為淵涵溥博而天德所由以立推之為敦
龐俊偉而王道所由以行古之帝王為能作
===
則於當時而施聲於後世良有以也而非有
輔德宣化之臣相與導迪而賛襄要亦不足
以臻此矣向使其知所以典學矣而或役志
於章句之末則吟呻佔畢以為博窮蒐廣覽
以為高雖講求日切而不識其要是學也而
非帝王之學也而況啓誘無其資德亦奚由
而崇乎使其知所以勤政矣而或從事於瑣
屑之務則繁目密網以為精纖析縷舉以為
察雖籌畫日詳而不得其綱是政也而非帝
王之政也而況䟽附無其助業亦奚由而廣

punctuated:
臣余孟麟。

臣對：臣聞帝王之建極以綏猷也，有立天下之大本，有圖天下之大機。大本者何？明義理以養其心，而典學之為急；大機者何？擴紀法以經其治，而勤政之為先。然遜志時敏，允懷于茲，非古之所謂典學乎？而學之所當急者，貴識其要；宣序糾虔，朝夕無怠，非古之所謂勤政乎？而政之所當先者，貴得其綱。此則本之為淵涵溥博，而天德所由以立；推之為敦龐俊偉，而王道所由以行。古之帝王為能作則於當時，而施聲於後世，良有以也。而非有輔德宣化之臣相與導迪而賛襄，要亦不足以臻此矣。向使其知所以典學矣，而或役志於章句之末，則吟呻佔畢以為博，窮蒐廣覽以為高，雖講求日切，而不識其要，是學也，而非帝王之學也，而況啓誘無其資，德亦奚由而崇乎？使其知所以勤政矣，而或從事於瑣屑之務，則繁目密網以為精，纖析縷舉以為察，雖籌畫日詳，而不得其綱，是政也，而非帝王之政也，而況䟽附無其助，業亦奚由而廣
translation_en:
Your servant Yu Menglin 余孟麟.

Your servant replies: Your servant has heard that when emperors and kings establish the supreme standard so as to pacify and guide the way of governance, there is the establishing of the great foundation of the realm, and there is the planning for the great pivot of the realm. What is the great foundation? It is to clarify moral principles in order to nourish one's mind, taking devotion to learning as the urgent task. What is the great pivot? It is to broaden laws and regulations in order to order one's governance, taking diligence in administration as the first priority. Yet, "to be humble in will and ever diligent, sincerely cherishing this"—is this not what the ancients called devotion to learning? And in that which learning ought to treat as urgent, the value lies in recognizing its essentials. To proclaim order and correct with reverence, unremitting morning and evening—is this not what the ancients called diligence in administration? And in that which administration ought to put first, the value lies in grasping its guiding threads. In this way, rooted inside, it becomes deep, all-embracing, and vast, whereby heavenly virtue is established; extended outward, it becomes generous, grand, and magnificent, whereby the kingly way is put into practice. That the emperors and kings of antiquity were able to set the standard for their own times and project their renown to later generations was truly for this reason. Yet without ministers who assist in virtue and propagate transformation to guide, enlighten, and aid them together, they after all would not have been able to attain this. Suppose a ruler knows how to devote himself to learning, yet perhaps enslaves his mind to the trivialities of chapter and verse—chanting over texts and tablets and taking that to be erudition, exhaustively collecting and widely perusing and taking that to be loftiness; even if his study and inquiry grow more earnest by the day, if he does not recognize its essentials, this is mere learning, and not the learning of emperors and kings. How much more so when, lacking the resource of inspiring guidance, by what means could his virtue be exalted? Suppose he knows how to be diligent in administration, yet perhaps busies himself with petty and trivial affairs—multiplying items and tightening the net of rules and taking that to be precision, splitting hairs and enumerating threads and taking that to be discernment; even if his planning grows more detailed by the day, if he does not grasp its guiding threads, this is mere administration, and not the administration of emperors and kings. How much more so when, lacking the assistance of ministers who rally subjects from afar and near, by what means could his enterprise be broadened…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
乎知此則以之為學天下所以稱善學也以
之為政天下所以稱善政也懿美之德何有
於不立而棊隆之化何有於不溥者哉欽惟
皇帝陛下
英資天授
聖學日新應帝王五百歲之昌期而光膺
寶命延
祖宗億萬年之正統而不振
瑶圖
經筵日講之禮益懋於緝熙
===
召對晉接之儀每勤於輔弼
念事機之叢脞則湔宿垢以釐群工懼士習之
澆漓則崇正學以一眾志是以百嘉鬯遂四
海敉寧凡在逖聰垂聲孰不樂觀乎盛事而
蘄效於
熈朝哉此盖學識其要矣政得其綱矣乃於
萬幾之暇進臣等於
廷而賜之
清問惓惓乎以典學勤政為務臣有以仰窺
陛下望道未見求治無已之盛心矣臣竊伏草莽

punctuated: 乎？知此，則以之為學，天下所以稱善學也；以之為政，天下所以稱善政也。懿美之德何有於不立，而棊隆之化何有於不溥者哉？欽惟皇帝陛下，英資天授，聖學日新，應帝王五百歲之昌期而光膺寶命，延祖宗億萬年之正統而不振瑶圖。經筵日講之禮，益懋於緝熙；召對晉接之儀，每勤於輔弼。念事機之叢脞，則湔宿垢以釐群工；懼士習之澆漓，則崇正學以一眾志。是以百嘉鬯遂，四海敉寧，凡在逖聰垂聲，孰不樂觀乎盛事，而蘄效於熈朝哉？此盖學識其要矣，政得其綱矣，乃於萬幾之暇，進臣等於廷，而賜之清問，惓惓乎以典學勤政為務。臣有以仰窺陛下望道未見、求治無已之盛心矣。臣竊伏草莽，
translation_en:
…? If one understands this, then when applied to learning, it is what all under Heaven praises as good learning; when applied to governance, it is what all under Heaven praises as good governance. How could admirable and fine virtue fail to be established, and how could a foundational and flourishing transformation fail to be universally extended?

Reverently I reflect that Your Majesty the Emperor is endowed by Heaven with heroic talent, and Your sage learning is daily renewed. Answering the prosperous cycle of five hundred years for true kings, You gloriously received the precious Mandate; extending the legitimate succession of Your ancestors for myriad years, You grandly [?] rouse the imperial plan. In the rites of the Classics Mat and Daily Lectures, You exert Yourself ever more in continuing luminosity; in the ceremonies of summoning for audience and receiving in person, You are ever diligent with Your輔弼 [Grand Secretaries and chief ministers]. Mindful of the petty complexities of state affairs, You wash away old impurities to regulate the百官 [officialdom]; fearing the thinness and decadence of literati customs, You exalt orthodox learning to unify the minds of the multitude. Therefore, a hundred blessings flourish and reach fulfillment, and the Four Seas are pacified and tranquil. Among all who hear from afar and listen to the echoes [?], who does not rejoice to witness these grand affairs and aspire to render service to this resplendent court? This is indeed because in learning You have recognized its essentials, and in governance You have grasped its overarching principles. Yet now, in the leisure from a myriad state affairs, You have advanced Your servants to the court and bestowed upon us Your pure inquiry, earnestly taking devotion to learning and diligence in governance as Your priority. Your servant is thus able to look up and glimpse Your Majesty's grand heart, which gazes toward the Way as though not yet having seen it and seeks good governance without cease. Your servant, having lived humbly in the countryside,…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
久懷芹曝之私乃今
休命所及臣敢不披瀝以對嘗聞書之言君也
曰天子惟君萬邦其言臣也曰良臣惟聖蓋
泰運起而上下志同德意流而古今道合都
俞吁咈之風倡于其前而靖獻箴規之義衍
于其後是惟辟惟賢自古記之矣唐虞以往
姑勿論論其嗣服之初所為典學而勤政者
如伊尹之訓太甲曰王懋乃德無時逸豫傅
說之望高宗曰學于古訓道積厥躬而成王
訪落之詩有曰紹庭上下陟降厥家周公無
===
逸之訓有曰天命自度不敢荒寧其所以言
學言政者蓋備矣乃今頌商周之盛所以上
稱一代之明君而下稱一代之碩輔者豈無
自哉嗣是而後知學之當務與治之當圖者
非不代有其人也然以之考德而其德不能
遠紹於前修雖著作不無可觀亦詞章之習
耳何以成經緯之能以之論治而其治不能
比隆於先烈雖建立不無可紀亦粉飾之具
耳何以弘參贊之用此其故何也勉強以求
道學非不典也而未知其所當急是以几杖

punctuated: 久懷芹曝之私，乃今休命所及，臣敢不披瀝以對？嘗聞《書》之言君也，曰：「天子惟君萬邦。」其言臣也，曰：「良臣惟聖。」蓋泰運起而上下志同，德意流而古今道合，都俞吁咈之風倡于其前，而靖獻箴規之義衍于其後，是惟辟惟賢，自古記之矣。唐虞以往，姑勿論；論其嗣服之初，所為典學而勤政者：如伊尹之訓太甲曰：「王懋乃德，無時逸豫。」傅說之望高宗曰：「學于古訓，道積厥躬。」而成王《訪落》之詩有曰：「紹庭上下，陟降厥家。」周公《無逸》之訓有曰：「天命自度，不敢荒寧。」其所以言學、言政者，蓋備矣。乃今頌商、周之盛，所以上稱一代之明君，而下稱一代之碩輔者，豈無自哉？嗣是而後，知學之當務與治之當圖者，非不代有其人也。然以之考德，而其德不能遠紹於前修，雖著作不無可觀，亦詞章之習耳，何以成經緯之能？以之論治，而其治不能比隆於先烈，雖建立不無可紀，亦粉飾之具耳，何以弘參贊之用？此其故何也？勉強以求道，學非不典也，而未知其所當急，是以几杖
translation_en:
…and have long harbored a humble desire to offer what little I have; now that Your gracious command has reached me, how could Your servant dare not pour out his heart in reply?

I have heard that when the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of the ruler, it says: "The Son of Heaven is the sovereign of the myriad states." And when it speaks of the minister, it says: "The good minister renders his sovereign sage." Indeed, when an era of great prosperity arises, superior and inferior share the same purpose; when virtuous intent flows forth, ancient and modern ways converge. The spirit of harmonious affirmation and frank remonstrance was initiated beforehand, and the principle of loyal dedication and admonitory counsel was elaborated thereafter—thus, that it depends on both the sovereign and the worthy ministers has been recorded since antiquity.

Leaving aside the eras of Tang and Yu and earlier, let us discuss those who, upon first succeeding to the throne, devoted themselves to constant study and diligent governance: for instance, Yi Yin instructed Tai Jia, saying, "May the King strive in his virtue, and never indulge in ease and pleasure"; Fu Yue looked in hope to Gaozong, saying, "Learn from the ancient precepts, and the Way will accumulate in your person." Moreover, in King Cheng's ode "Taking Counsel at the Beginning of Reign" (Fangluo), it says: "Continuing the ways of the court above and below, ascending and descending in the house." And in the Duke of Zhou's instruction "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi), it says: "Measuring himself by the Mandate of Heaven, he dared not give himself over to idle tranquility." What they said regarding learning and governance was indeed comprehensive. When today we praise the flourishing ages of Shang and Zhou, calling those above the enlightened rulers of an era and those below the great辅佐 (coadjutors) of an era, how could this be without reason?

From that time onward, no dynasty lacked men who understood that learning must be pursued and governance must be planned. Yet if we examine their virtue by this standard, their virtue could not reach back to match the former worthies; although their writings are not without merit, they are merely exercises in literary ornament—how could they achieve the ability to order the state? And if we judge their governance by this standard, their governance could not rival the splendor of past achievements; although their establishments are not unworthy of record, they are merely instruments of superficial embellishment—how could they broaden the function of assisting in cosmic transformation? What is the reason for this? When they forced themselves to seek the Way, their learning was not inconstant, yet they did not know what was most urgent; therefore, those who with stool and staff…

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
執業者徒親炙於桓榮更日侍讀者竟遷就
於馬禇而謂之識其要焉未也勵精以圖幾
政非不勤也而未知其所當先是以齋居决
事者毎崇尚乎刑名中夜咨詢者亦侈心於
禱祀而謂之得其綱焉未也其何以立天下
之大本而圖天下之大機也哉臣且請於
聖問之所疑者言之夜分講經於漢得光武焉歲
周太平御覽於宋得太宗焉隻日不費講讀
於宋得仁宗焉此其於學可謂篤矣則學之
不可已也而漢高祖之興造洪業也顧得之
===
馬上不事詩書乃學亦有時而可廢者無亦
闢乾定鼎當建創九服之初時則學或有所
不暇乎而不知政以顯其學彼之所以揮霍
而勘勦者孰非學之所發越也衡石程書於
秦得始皇焉衛士傳餐於隋得文帝焉汗透
御服日旰忘倦於唐得憲宗焉此其於政可
謂勤矣則政之不可已也而漢文帝之守成
致治也顧躬修玄默清靜無為乃政亦有時
而可弛者無亦歌雍詠勺乗百年禮樂之會
時則政或有所不必煩乎而不知學以基其

執業者徒親炙於桓榮更日侍讀者竟遷就
於馬褚而謂之識其要焉未也勵精以圖幾
政非不勤也而未知其所當先是以齋居決
事者每崇尚乎刑名中夜咨詢者亦侈心於
禱祀而謂之得其綱焉未也其何以立天下
之大本而圖天下之大機也哉臣且請於
聖問之所疑者言之夜分講經於漢得光武焉歲
周太平御覽於宋得太宗焉隻日不費講讀
於宋得仁宗焉此其於學可謂篤矣則學之
不可已也而漢高祖之興造洪業也顧得之
===
馬上不事詩書乃學亦有時而可廢者無亦
闕乾定鼎當建創九服之初時則學或有所
不暇乎而不知政以顯其學彼之所以揮霍
而勵勸者執非學之所發越也衡石程書於
秦得始皇焉衛士傳餐於隋得文帝焉汗透
御服日旰忘倦於唐得憲宗焉此其於政可
謂勤矣則政之不可已也而漢文帝之守成
致治也顧躬修玄默清靜無為乃政亦有時
而可弛者無亦歌雍詠勺乘百年禮樂之會
時則政或有所不必煩乎而不知學以基其

Exerting one's spirit to plan the subtle springs of governance is not lacking in diligence in administration, yet they did not know what should come first. Therefore, the one who decided affairs while dwelling in fasting abstinence [like Emperor Xuan of Han] constantly esteemed legalism and penal names; and the one who made inquiries in the middle of the night [like Emperor Wen of Han] also indulged his mind in prayers and sacrifices—to say that they obtained the guiding principles is not yet so. How then could they establish the great foundation of the world and plan the great枢機 (pivotal springs) of the world? Your servant begs to speak further regarding the doubts raised in Your Majesty's sacred question. For lecturing on the Classics until midnight, in the Han we find Emperor Guangwu 光武; for reading through the Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era (Taiping yulan 太平御覽) in the course of a year, in the Song we find Emperor Taizong 太宗; for not letting even odd-numbered days pass without lectures and readings, in the Song we find Emperor Renzong 仁宗. These rulers may be called earnest in their learning, which shows that learning cannot be ceased. Yet when Emperor Gaozu 高祖 of Han raised and created his vast enterprise, he nonetheless won it on horseback and did not occupy himself with the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) and the Book of Documents (Shu 書). Could it be that learning may at times be dispensed with—perhaps because, when opening up Heaven and settling the dynastic tripods at the very beginning of founding the Nine Domains, the times left no leisure for learning? Yet people do not realize that governance manifests one's learning: in his sweeping command and his suppression and pacification of rivals, what part of it was not the outward expression of learning? For weighing documents by the stone-weight to set a daily quota, in the Qin we find the First Emperor 始皇; for having palace guards pass in his meals, in the Sui we find Emperor Wen 文帝; for sweat soaking through the imperial robes and forgetting fatigue until late in the day, in the Tang we find Emperor Xianzong 憲宗. These rulers may be called diligent in their governance, which shows that governance cannot be ceased. Yet when Emperor Wen 文帝 of Han preserved the dynastic achievements and brought about order, he nonetheless personally cultivated profound silence and practiced pure tranquility and non-action. title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
政彼之所以謙讓而默運者孰非政之所化
哉也然則學之與政果可以偏廢耶惟我
皇上茂齡御極治理維新
臨涖以来講學親賢寒暑不輟而天下之大本
以正辨色偸盥日出
視政而天下之大機以弘即詩書所稱且將遠
邁矣而於我
二祖
八宗之丕緒不亦有光哉然德已盛而猶以為未
盛化已隆而猶以為未隆乃又
===
詢臣等以學之所以急政之所以先顧臣愚昧
何足以知之載觀程顥之論學也謂帝王之
學不在於章句盖識其要也而學之所以急
者胥是矣荀卿之論政也謂主好要則百事
詳盖得其綱也而政之所以先者胥是矣然
學在君也而所以翼其德者則臣也政在君
也而所以賛其化者則臣也故古昔盛時君
有造膝而語有拊髀而思者孰不倚重於臣
乎臣有遇巷而通有持籌而畫者孰不陳謨
於君乎是故仲舒之在漢武則有賢良之策
alt_text:
政彼之所以謙讓而默運者孰非政之所化
裁也然則學之與政果可以偏廢耶惟我
皇上茂齡御極治理維新
臨蒞以來講學親賢寒暑不輟而天下之大本
以正辨色舍盈日出
視政而天下之大機以弘即詩書所稱且將遠
邁矣而於我
===
二祖
八宗之丕緒不亦有光矣然德已盛而猶以為未
盛化已隆而猶以為未隆乃又
詢臣等以學之所以急政之所以先顧臣愚昧
何足以知之載觀程顥之論學也謂帝王之
學不在於章句蓋識其要也而學之所以急
者胥是矣荀卿之論政也謂主好要則百事
詳蓋得其綱也而政之所以先者胥是矣然
學在君也而所以翼其德者則臣也政在君
也而所以贊其化者則臣也故古昔盛時君
有造膝而語有排闥而思者孰不倚重於臣
乎臣有遇巷而通有持籌而畫者孰不陳謨
於君乎是故仲舒之在漢武則有賢良之策
punctuated: 政，彼之所以謙讓而默運者，孰非政之所化哉也？然則學之與政，果可以偏廢耶？惟我皇上茂齡御極，治理維新。臨涖以来，講學親賢，寒暑不輟，而天下之大本以正；辨色偸盥，日出視政，而天下之大機以弘。即《詩》、《書》所稱，且將遠邁矣，而於我二祖、八宗之丕緒，不亦有光哉？然德已盛而猶以為未盛，化已隆而猶以為未隆，乃又詢臣等以學之所以急、政之所以先。顧臣愚昧，何足以知之？載觀程顥之論學也，謂帝王之學不在於章句，盖識其要也，而學之所以急者胥是矣；荀卿之論政也，謂主好要則百事詳，盖得其綱也，而政之所以先者胥是矣。然學在君也，而所以翼其德者則臣也；政在君也，而所以賛其化者則臣也。故古昔盛時，君有造膝而語、有拊髀而思者，孰不倚重於臣乎？臣有遇巷而通、有持籌而畫者，孰不陳謨於君乎？是故仲舒之在漢武，則有賢良之策；
translation_en:
… governance: is not that by which he practiced modesty and yielding and operated silently all the transforming effect of governance [reading 哉 as 裁]? This being so, can learning and governance indeed be emphasized one at the expense of the other?

Our August Emperor ascended the throne in his flourishing youth, renewing the order of governance. Since coming to rule, he has expounded upon learning and drawn close to the worthy without ceasing through winter cold and summer heat, and thus the great foundation of the realm is rectified; as the sky grows light enough to discern colors he washes [? 偸盥], and at sunrise he attends to governance, and thus the great pivot of the realm is broadened. Even what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) will soon be far surpassed; and does this not also bring glory to the grand patrimony of our Two Progenitors and Eight Ancestors? Yet though his virtue is already abundant, he still regards it as not yet abundant; though his transforming influence is already lofty, he still regards it as not yet lofty, and so he further inquiries of us, his servants, as to what is urgent in learning and what comes first in governance.

Yet ignorant and benighted as your servant is, how could I be adequate to know this? When we further examine Cheng Hao's 程顥 discourse on learning, he said that the learning of emperors and kings does not lie in chapter and phrase, for he recognized its essentials; and all that is urgent in learning is right here. When Xun Qing 荀卿 [Xunzi] discoursed on governance, he said that if the ruler loves the essentials then the hundred affairs will be attended to in detail, for he grasped its guiding rope; and all that comes first in governance is right here.

Yet learning rests with the ruler, while those who assist his virtue are the ministers; governance rests with the ruler, while those who aid his transforming influence are the ministers. Therefore, in the flourishing ages of antiquity, among rulers there were those who drew close knee-to-knee to converse, and those who slapped their thighs in longing thought—which of them did not rely heavily upon his ministers? Among ministers there were those who achieved mutual understanding as if meeting in a narrow lane [cf. Odes, "Yu xiang"], and those who held the counting-tallies to plan—which of them did not set forth counsels before his ruler? Therefore, when Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 served under Emperor Wu of Han 漢武, there were his policy essays as a Worthy and Good candidate; …

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
王吉之在神爵則有變俗之言而審尚治性
勸學則匡衡之上於元帝也貢禹之在初元
則有節儉之戒陳寵之在建初則有蕩滌煩
苛之語姚崇呂公著則各以十事進司馬光
則獨以三劄陳而稽古正學定志則程子之
獻於神宗也語學則凡志氣之所勤惰詩書
之所討論成法之所遵守徑竇之所移易罔
不感發而勸戒矣語政則凡風俗之所隆汚
紀綱之所因革賢否之所進退民物之所甄
陶罔不周密而詳盡矣此其與君之典學圖
===
政未必無裨使其君傾心而聽之審時而行
之又何治之不古若也奈何以宴安為志者
雖正心誠意之說而不免厭聞以既效滿心
者雖近利小康之治而不免苟就君之待臣
與臣之責君又安望其相得而章也哉夫古
今一心也創守一道也宜於古者未有不宜
於今而舍是則非殷誥周官之典矣善於創
者未有不善於守而舍是則非車攻吉日之
休矣
聖問乃欲折衷衆論究其指歸而臣復何言哉惟

punctuated: 王吉之在神爵，則有變俗之言；而審尚治性、勸學，則匡衡之上於元帝也。貢禹之在初元，則有節儉之戒；陳寵之在建初，則有蕩滌煩苛之語。姚崇、呂公著，則各以十事進；司馬光則獨以三劄陳；而稽古正學定志，則程子之獻於神宗也。語學，則凡志氣之所勤惰，詩書之所討論，成法之所遵守，徑竇之所移易，罔不感發而勸戒矣；語政，則凡風俗之所隆汚，紀綱之所因革，賢否之所進退，民物之所甄陶，罔不周密而詳盡矣。此其與君之典學圖政，未必無裨。使其君傾心而聽之，審時而行之，又何治之不古若也？奈何以宴安為志者，雖正心誠意之說，而不免厭聞；以既效滿心者，雖近利小康之治，而不免苟就。君之待臣，與臣之責君，又安望其相得而章也哉？夫古今一心也，創守一道也。宜於古者，未有不宜於今，而舍是則非《殷誥》、《周官》之典矣；善於創者，未有不善於守，而舍是則非《車攻》、《吉日》之休矣。聖問乃欲折衷衆論，究其指歸，而臣復何言哉？惟
translation_en: … Wang Ji 王吉 in the Shenjue era (61–58 BCE) offered words on reforming customs; and as for examining what is valued, cultivating one's nature, and encouraging learning, those were presented by Kuang Heng 匡衡 to Emperor Yuan. Gong Yu 貢禹 in the Chuyuan era (48–44 BCE) offered admonitions on frugality; Chen Chong 陳寵 in the Jianchu era (76–84 CE) offered words on sweeping away vexatious harshness. Yao Chong 姚崇 and Lü Gongzhu 呂公著 each presented ten matters; Sima Guang 司馬光 alone set forth three memorials; and as for examining antiquity, rectifying learning, and fixing the will, those were offered by Master Cheng 程子 (Cheng Hao 程顥) to Emperor Shenzong. When speaking of learning, regarding everything wherein the will and spirit are diligent or indolent, what the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu) discuss, what established laws are to be observed, and what shortcuts and loopholes shift and alter the mind, there was nothing in which they did not inspire and admonish. When speaking of governance, regarding everything wherein customs flourish or decay, how institutions and laws are continued or reformed, how the worthy and unworthy are advanced or dismissed, and how the people and things are molded and fashioned, there was nothing in which they were not thorough and exhaustive. All this was not without benefit to the ruler's devotion to learning and planning for governance. Had their rulers inclined their hearts to listen to them and examined the times to put them into practice, how could their governance have failed to equal antiquity? Yet how is it that those who set their minds on ease and comfort cannot avoid growing weary of hearing even doctrines on rectifying the mind and making the intentions sincere, and those whose hearts are satisfied with results already achieved cannot avoid carelessly settling for governance of immediate profit and minor tranquility? In how the ruler treats his ministers and how the ministers hold their ruler to account, how then could one hope for them to complement each other and shine forth? Now, antiquity and the present share a single mind; founding and preserving share a single Way. What was suitable for antiquity has never been unsuitable for the present, and to abandon this is no longer the canon of the Announcements of Yin (Yin gao) and the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan); what is good for founding has never failed to be good for preserving, and to abandon this is no longer the excellence of the odes "Our Chariots Were Strong" (Che gong) and "An Auspicious Day" (Ji ri). title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
考先聖之術察當世之務為
陛下陳之夫典學之急急於識其要矣今講讀諸
臣循次而進展卷而陳非不秩秩然有章也
然講有定期書有定限則德性未易以涵養
氣質未易以陶鎔請於
聽講之餘使諸臣各得以從容進勸隨事納規如
范氏善惡之說其本在君心所養可也如朱
子誠敬之勉其要在聖心克正可也而所謂
識其要者不在是乎立政之先先於得其綱
矣今府部諸臣率屬而治按牘而行非不井
===
井然有叙也然天澤禮嚴堂陛分隔則悃誠
未易以展輸情誼未易以交洽請於
視朝之後使諸臣各得以陳說利病敷納謀猷
如韓琦每日奏對務竭忠誠以裨實政可也
如魏相每於御前必條述故事以救時弊可
也而所謂得其綱者不在是乎是故好文盛
事也而程頤乃謂帝王之學不在文義崇儉
美德也而柳公權乃謂天子之儉乃其末節
區畫庶務人皆以為勤也而杜黃裳乃謂人
主不親細務威振四夷人皆以為武也而胡

… examine the arts of the former sages and observe the affairs of the present age, and set them forth for Your Majesty.

Now, the urgency of pursuing constant study lies in recognizing its essentials. Today the various exposition and reading officials advance in turn, unroll the texts, and set forth their explanations; it is not that this lacks orderly pattern. Yet because lectures have fixed schedules and the texts have set limits, one's moral nature is not easily nourished and one's temperament is not easily molded. I beg that in the leisure after attending the lectures, you allow the various officials each to offer unhurried exhortations and present remonstrances as matters arise: just as in Fan's [Fan Zuyu 范祖禹] discourse on good and evil, where the root lies in what the ruler's mind nourishes—that would do; and just as in Master Zhu's [Zhu Xi 朱熹] encouragement of sincerity and reverence, where the essential point lies in the sage's mind being able to rectify itself—that too would do. Does not what is called recognizing the essentials lie right here?

The priority in establishing governance lies in grasping its guiding threads. Today the officials of the Chief Military Commissions and the Six Ministries lead their subordinates in administration and act according to the documents; it is not that this lacks methodical order. Yet because the ritual between heaven and marsh is strict and the hall and steps are kept apart, sincere devotion is not easily poured forth and feelings of fellowship are not easily harmonized. I beg that after holding court, you allow the various officials each to set forth advantages and abuses and present their plans and counsels: just as Han Qi 韓琦 in his daily audiences strove to exhaust his loyalty and sincerity to aid practical governance—that would do; and just as Wei Xiang 魏相 whenever before the imperial presence invariably cited precedents point by point to remedy the abuses of the age—that too would do. Does not what is called grasping the guiding threads lie right here?

translation_en: …Yin 胡寅 nonetheless said that a sage king does not toil over distant campaigns. Is this not because learning has what is urgent, and governance has what comes first? Your servant has still more to say. A tree that reaches the skies springs from a tender shoot; the currents of the deep sea are formed from trickling drops—this speaks of gradual accumulation. Your Majesty is daily more diligent in learning, yet could there not be subtle lapses interrupting it? Surely, at the stirring of a single thought, it should be as if facing the divine spirits; at the undertaking of a single action, as if the Grand Preceptor and Grand Guardian were present. Spacious halls and fine felt rugs are nothing less than places for accumulating learning; charts on the left and histories on the right are nothing less than starting points for advancing in learning. Thus learning will grow ever more thorough and provide an ample foundation for carrying out governance; it is learning, yet none of it is not governance. In raising a mound of nine ren, one may fall short by a single basket of earth; in traveling a hundred li, ninety is only halfway—this speaks of how few see things through to the end. Your Majesty is daily more industrious in governance, yet could negligence and idleness not take advantage of it? Surely, in issuing commands and ordinances there must be far-reaching plans; in establishing principles and setting forth regulations there must be distant forethought. Deeply nurture the source of transformation, without taking dense notes and rapid beats as true music; set up standards for all things, without taking galloping at full speed with tightened reins as true charioteering. Thus governance will grow ever more expansive and put the substance of constant learning into practice; it is governance, yet none of it is not learning. Your servant has also examined why the rulers of the Shang and Zhou were able to achieve glorious restorations and return to great vigor: it was not only that their virtue was strengthened through enlightenment and instruction, and their Way exalted through grand plans and achievements. text:

鏡然後揆事宰物廓然無滯此心得其養所
以為務學之典刑也其言政則有曰朕念創
業之艱難日不暇食坐不安枕又曰人君日
理萬幾怠心一生則庶務壅滯其患不可勝

加其膏而希其光而其光為益著矣法此以

…and goes forth and comes in with the workings of vital force; to hold fast to it and preserve it is difficult." And they also say: "When this mind is like still water and a bright mirror, only then can it measure affairs and govern things, vast and clear without obstruction." This attainment of nourishment for the mind is what serves as the model and standard for devoting oneself to learning. When they speak of governance, they say: "We reflect upon the hardships of founding the dynasty, having no leisure to eat by day and sitting without resting comfortably on Our pillow." And they also say: "A ruler attends to ten thousand affairs each day; as soon as an indolent thought arises, general affairs become clogged and obstructed, and the resulting harm is beyond words." This accomplishment of affairs through diligence is what serves as the carpenter's square and rule for establishing governance.

Your servant wishes that Your Majesty take this as a model for learning, inscribing admonitions and cautions, whereby You may ascend to the greatness of the ancient predecessors—just like adding oil in hopes of brightness, whereby the light becomes all the more manifest; and that You take this as a model for governance, being cautious at the beginning and planning for the end, whereby You may bring about the peaceful and vast governance of antiquity—just like dredging the source to extend the stream, whereby the flow becomes all the longer. From this, ancient and modern will share the same mind, the enlightened ruler and worthy ministers will unite in virtue, and wherever harmonious vital force reaches, both the court and the provinces will be filled to overflowing. In the flourishing of governing achievements, spirits and men will rejoice in harmony, and altogether You will rival the splendor and compare in merit with the rulers of the Shang and Zhou dynasties! As for those of the Han, Tang, and Song, how could their paltriness even be worth counting? Your servant has offended the imperial majesty and is overcome with extreme trembling and fear of falling short. Your servant respectfully replies.

title: 萬曆二年進士登科錄
text:
臣王應選
臣對臣聞帝王之所以憲天而立德者學也
然必有純心之功而後天下之化源以端帝
王之所以法天而立道者政也然必有用賢
之益而後天下之化機以普夫天之宰萬物
也豈徒以其氣乎必有德焉以樞紐於無端
矣而帝王者將以繼天之志焉則典學以懋
純王之體者何可巳也天之運萬物也豈徒
以其形乎必有道焉以隆施於不匱矣而帝
王者將以述天之事焉則勤政以達純王之
===
用者何可巳也學以立聖政之本而後政之
行也為實功然徒學而不得其所以典學之
要則化何由端政以顯聖學之用而後學之
修也為實德然徒政而不得其所以立政之
機則化何由普是故句讀佔畢非帝王之學
也必多識畜德以養此心而宥密淵微之地
粹然無一念之疵然後與天合德而天下之
治本以善程功計能非帝王之政也必推誠
盡下以任賢臣而手足腹心之交藹然無一
毫之間然後與天合道而天下之治功以成
